articles.title: Soft robotic and computational models of left atrial hemodynamics in sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation
Topological Josephson trijunctions as a Majorana source and path
articles.abstract: Abstract Majorana bound states (MBSs) are zero-energy localized states in topological superconductors, obeying non-Abelian braiding statistics. Manipulation of mobile MBSs, encompassing their on-demand generation, propagation, and fusion, is essential for braiding MBSs and operating topological qubits. We show that the manipulation is enabled by a trijunction formed on a topological insulator in a perpendicular magnetic field, where three Josephson junctions meet. While the superconducting phases at the trijunction center evolve to cross a boundary between topological and non-topological phase domains, the trijunction offers two distinct dynamics, source/sink and path, depending on the phase boundaries. At a source/sink boundary, two MBSs are pairwise generated at the center, and one of them is ejected to a Josephson junction. The reverse, pair annihilation by collision of two MBSs, can also happen. At a path boundary, an MBS moves from a Josephson junction to the trijunction center or vice versa, without involving other MBSs. Exploiting the two dynamics, fusion and braiding of MBSs can be operated in a trijunction network. We illustrate this with a double trijunction setup, where non-Abelian state evolutions associated with MBSs can be manipulated without dynamical control of the setup and detected by Josephson emission spectroscopy.

Mapping Future Energy Journeys Through Modeling the Global Transport of Synthetic Energy Carriers
articles.abstract: Abstract Synthetic energy carriers can connect renewable-energy-rich potential production regions with distant demand centers, but the emergence of trade depends on total supply costs. Here, we develop a spatially resolved heuristic combining hydrogen production costs with ports, pipelines, and shipping routes, as well as syntheses, cracking, and reformation processes, to identify key import corridors. Across 10,883 production locations and seven different scenarios, we find that export regions connected to the importer through retrofit-ready pipelines remain competitive despite only moderate renewable potentials. Meanwhile, for remote exporters competitiveness depends on port availability and coastal access through pipeline networks. Gaseous hydrogen dominates short pipeline routes, and ammonia is preferred for maritime trade, whereas methanol and methane emerge in long multimodal chains. Additional results show that low-cost heat availability is required for the competitiveness of liquid organic hydrogen carriers, while accounting for market values of conventional counterparts boosts ammonia and methanol trade.

articles.title: Antagonistic second-messenger signalling coordinates Pseudomonas aeruginosa surface colonization and virulence
articles.abstract: Abstract Efficient colonisation of host tissue surfaces is a prerequisite for bacterial infection. In the human pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa , the second messengers cAMP and c-di-GMP regulate surface behaviours and virulence, but how these pathways are coordinated during tissue infection has remained unclear. Here we demonstrate that cAMP and c-di-GMP establish mutually exclusive signalling states at the single-cell level, generating distinct subpopulations of motile and surface-attached cells through pathway-specific control of type IV pili (T4P). Initial surface contact triggers an increase in c-di-GMP, activating FimW and driving stable attachment via bipolar T4P formation. This state is progressively replaced by cAMP, which inactivates FimW-dependent attachment and induces FimX-mediated T4P polarisation, surface motility and virulence activation. The resulting signalling transition enforces coexisting subpopulations, with attached cells gradually displaced by spreading cells. Using a human airway tissue model, we show that both T4P-mediated adhesion and twitching motility are required for invasion and tissue damage. Based on this, we propose that reciprocal cAMP–c-di-GMP signalling coordinates complementary T4P functions to optimise P. aeruginosa surface colonisation and infection.

articles.title: Ultra-high precision speckle spectrometer enabling radio-frequency scale resolution of atomic spectra
articles.abstract: Abstract Laser speckle, the granular intensity pattern arising from random optical interference, provides a high-dimensional encoding of spectral information that can be exploited for precision metrology. Speckle-based spectrometers have advanced rapidly owing to their compact footprint, mechanical robustness and alignment agnostic nature, yet their spectral resolution has remained limited to the picometre scale. In this work, we break this limit by employing an integrating sphere as a multiply scattering cavity with access to a high range of path lengths to enhance spectral sensitivity. At 780 nm, the resulting device achieves a resolution of 6 fm, corresponding to a resolving power of 1.3 × 10 8 , representing an approximately 80-fold improvement over previous implementations. This ultra-high resolution enables clear discrimination of laser sidebands generated by an electro-optical modulator, with extracted sideband powers agreeing with expected values to within 1%. It further permits a direct speckle-based measurement of the hyperfine structure of the D 2 transition in 85 Rb, with transmission spectra differing by no more than 3.7% from independent wavemeter-referenced measurements. These results establish speckle as a platform for ultra-high precision spectroscopy, radio-frequency spectrometry, and microwave photonics.

articles.title: CO2 responsive nanoscopic and macroscopic materials directed by peptides
Nanofluid wetting of Cu enables thin lithium negative electrodes for high-energy and long-cycling lithium metal batteries
articles.abstract: Abstract Exploiting thin Li foils ≤ 20 μm is required for high-energy-density and long-cycling-lifespan battery, but is severely hindered by the poor processability of Li, as well as its inhomogeneous plating behaviors and resulting low Coulombic efficiency. Herein, an approach balancing Li supply and consumption is fulfilled by designing thin molten-salt-derived, nanocomposite Li@LiX metal negative electrodes. Benefitting from the formation of nanofluid due to the spontaneous reaction of inorganic nanoparticles in molten Li, the bonding states at both Li surface and Li|Cu interface are effectively regulated, displaying an enhanced wetting behaviour of Li on Cu. This approach enables the fabrication of an 800-nm-thick Li-based negative electrode foil as well as the formation of an inorganic-rich interphase upon cycling, which suppresses Li consumption by reducing corrosion susceptibility. As a result, practical pouch cells composed of 10-μm-thick Li@lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) and LiFePO 4 offer stable cycling over 250 cycles, while those composed of 20-μm-thick Li@LiFSI and LiNi 0.92 Co 0.03 Mn 0.05 O 2 with an areal capacity of 4.6 mAh cm −2 achieve 100 cycles, yielding specific energy of 498 Wh kg −1 and energy density of 1,142 Wh L −1 , indicating that this design strategy is applicable to lithium metal batteries.

articles.title: Insular motor and error encoding supports self-correcting intracranial brain-computer interface
articles.abstract: Abstract Error recognition is fundamental to adaptive behavior, enabling rapid compensatory action when outcomes deviate from expectations. Central to this function are neural circuits for performance monitoring, encoding cognitive signals that could support more reliable neural interfaces. Here, we recorded intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) in epilepsy patients to enable a motor brain-computer interface (BCI) while sampling error-related activity across a distributed network. Our work reveals high-frequency population dynamics emerging in the anterior insula and propagating to the prefrontal cortex as the interface fails to follow the user’s intention. We identify spatially organized insular responses to error processing and movement feedback, highlighting it as a heterogeneous hub linking action and outcome. Frontoinsular recording sites were found to preferentially encode error-related activity, while centroparietal responses were intermixed with compensatory motor signals, making the former a compelling target for real-time error correction. Together, our findings demonstrate a human intracranial BCI harnessing insular brain activity, integrating cognitive processes directly into device control.

articles.title:
Nonlinear Ozone-Phytoplankton-Sea-Ice
Coupling Regulates
Fine-Scale Gaseous Elemental Mercury Enhancement in the Arctic Marginal
Ice Zone
articles.abstract: Abstract Arctic marginal ice zone (MIZ) is a key summertime source of elevated atmospheric gaseous elemental mercury (GEM), but controls on its spatial variability remain unclear. Multiscale spatial statistics, machine learning, and quantile regression were applied to MOSAiC in situ observations (June-September 2020). GEM exhibits strong fine-scale spatial autocorrelation at 10 km (Moran’s I = 0.876). Random forest model (R2 = 0.85) with SHAP attribution identified ozone (O3), chlorophyll a (Chla), and open water fraction (OWF) as dominant GEM predictors. Quantile regression revealed that nonlinear coupling among OWF, Chla, and O3 strengthens under high GEM concentrations. By further combining spatial analysis with quantile regression modeling, a GEM-sensitive region was identified (OWF = 0.156–0.404, Chla = 1.17–1.57 μg/L, O3 = 9.2–19.7 ppb); within this region, both the O3 × Chla and O3 × OWF interactions exhibited significant positive correlations. The positive effect of O3 × Chla persists across all regions, while the O3 × OWF coupling varies dynamically with the retreat of sea ice. O3 indirectly favors GEM accumulation via regulating phytoplankton, and sea-ice melt exerts stage-dependent modulation of atmospheric oxidizing capacity. This study identifies O3 as a critical MIZ mercury regulator, and embedding O3-mediated pathways in models improves GEM projections under Arctic warming.

articles.title:
Occurrence
and Environmental
Weathering of Agricultural
Microplastics on Beaches across Japan: Insights into Surface Mineralization
and Metal Binding
articles.abstract: Abstract We investigated the coastal occurrence and environmental weathering of microplastics derived from polymer-coated fertilizers (PCFs) across Japan. A field survey along the Japanese coastline revealed that PCF-derived microplastics are widely distributed on beaches throughout the country, indicating that agricultural microplastics have dispersed far beyond agricultural landscapes. Compositional analysis showed that these particles consist predominantly of polyolefins (∼70%) and polyurethanes (∼30%) and commonly exhibit oxidative degradation accompanied by iron enrichment. Bulk elemental analysis demonstrated positive correlations between iron and multiple heavy metals. Micro-X-ray fluorescence mapping using a focused 20-μm beam showed that chromium is heterogeneously distributed on the plastic surface and spatially associated with iron, while X-ray absorption spectroscopy indicated its occurrence in ferrihydrite-like phases or as chromite. Although detailed spectroscopic evidence was obtained from a single selected particle, the widespread occurrence of PCF-derived microplastics and their observed metal enrichment suggest that similar geochemical processes may occur at other coastal sites. By linking nationwide field observations with process-level characterization, this study shows that microplastics have the potential to transition from inert debris to geochemically reactive substrates after coastal deposition.

articles.title: Policy Analysis at ES&T : New Science, New Technologies, and New Policy Needs

Correction to “A
Multi-Model Assessment of
the Air Quality and Health Impacts of U.S. Energy Decarbonization”

Microbial
Influence on Corrosive Processes at the
Cast Iron-Bentonite Interface during 3.5 Years of Incubation at 37
and 70 °C
articles.abstract: Abstract Bentonite-based geotechnical barriers constitute currently an integral part of international disposal concepts of high-level radioactive waste in claystone and crystalline rock. Elevated temperature, canister corrosion, and metabolic activity of microorganisms can influence their performance. To study these effects on processes at the cast iron-bentonite interface, microcosms were incubated with two different bentonites (B27 and GMZ-001), synthetic Opalinus Clay pore water with a high water-to-bentonite ratio and cast iron plates at 37 and 70 °C over a period of 3.5 years. No microorganisms or nutrients were added to those naturally occurring in the applied materials. Cast iron surfaces in contact with GMZ-001 bentonite appeared strongly corroded, and secondary layer-like structures formed at both temperatures. Furthermore, an accelerated release of iron into the pore water, H2 generation, and gas pressure build-up were observed. In contrast, incubation with B27 bentonite at 37 °C resulted in less corroded cast iron surfaces covered with iron sulfides, which seemed to passivate the surface and led to lower iron release, H2 generation, and gas pressure build-up. Respective B27 microcosms were dominated by metabolically active sulfate-reducing bacteria that induced iron sulfide formation. This study shows that the corrosion behavior of cast iron and changes in geochemical parameters like pH and pore water composition depend on the applied bentonite, naturally occurring microorganisms, and temperature.

articles.title: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke: the BRETIS-TNK2 trial
Pre-bilaterian roots of the chordate body plan

Energy
Supply and Demand Coordination Can Advance
Both Climate Goals and Sustainable Development in the Global South
articles.abstract: Abstract Reconciling climate mitigation with sustainable development is a critical imperative in the Global South, where rising emissions coincide with persistent development deficits. Here, we develop an integrated assessment framework linking nationally determined contribution (NDC)-aligned supply-side, demand-side, and coordinated supply–demand policy packages to greenhouse-gas trajectories and a six-goal Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) scorecard. We show that supply-focused renewable expansion or demand-focused efficiency improves selected SDG-related dimensions but creates trade-offs involving energy-cost pressure, water use, and ecosystem protection. By comparison, an integrated supply–demand strategy maximizes the SDG score (69 versus 65 under REF in 2050), enhances clean-energy penetration and efficiency, and averts approximately 485,000 annual premature deaths in 2050 relative to REF. These findings highlight the potential of coordinated supply–demand strategies to reduce climate–SDG trade-offs across the Global South.

articles.title:
Building-Stock
Turnover Reshapes Mitigation Priorities
in China’s Building Sector
articles.abstract: Abstract China’s building sector is pivotal to the 2060 carbon-neutrality ambition, yet prospective assessments often insufficiently capture regional heterogeneity and life-cycle emission dynamics. Here, we develop a provincial-level dynamic framework integrating material flow analysis, life-cycle assessment, and machine-learning-informed parameter trajectories to project emissions through 2060. Under a business-as-usual (BAU) scenario, China’s building life-cycle emissions are projected to peak in 2031–2033, while carbon neutrality remains challenged by persistent pressures from both material use and building operations. These pressures arise from the existing stock, whose continued use sustains energy demand while increasing building retirements shift construction from stock growth to the replacement of retired buildings. Implementing a high-efficiency scenario with regionally differentiated deployment of material- and energy-efficiency strategies could reduce China’s building-sector life-cycle emissions by 90% in 2060 relative to the BAU scenario. Provincial analysis further reveals that similar overall mitigation potential masks substantial differences in the composition of effective mitigation portfolios, reflecting local building-stock and energy-use characteristics. To close the remaining gap, deeper operational decarbonization should be coupled with stock-management strategies that extend building lifetimes, avoid premature demolition, and prioritize renovation and reuse.

articles.title: ES&T Next 60 Years: Sustainability and Climate Change

Structure-Dependent
Maternal-Fetal Transfer and Fetal
Hepatic Accumulation of PFOA and Hexafluoropropylene Oxide (HFPO)-Based
Alternatives: Implications for Fetal Liver Metabolic Disruption
articles.abstract: Abstract Hexafluoropropylene oxide (HFPO)-based compounds have been increasingly adopted as replacements for legacy per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) such as perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), yet evidence on developmental toxicity remains limited. This study investigated structure-dependent maternal-fetal transfer, fetal tissue distribution, and hepatic effects of PFOA and four HFPO-based alternatives, including hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (HFPO-DA) and hexafluoropropylene oxide trimer acid (HFPO-TA) homologues, in gestational mice. All compounds were detected in maternal serum, fetal tissues, and amniotic fluid in a dose-dependent manner, but transplacental transfer efficiencies varied markedly. C9 HFPO-TA showed the greatest fetal accumulation, indicating enhanced fetal retention. Desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry imaging revealed preferential hepatic localization of PFOA and HFPO trimers, with fetal hepatic burden increasing with van der Waals volume, suggesting structure-dependent enrichment. Metabolomics showed broad alterations of fetal hepatic metabolism, dominated by altered lipids and lipid-like molecules. 5-Aminolevulinic acid, a key heme precursor, was consistently reduced, whereas ALAS1 and ALAD protein levels increased, indicating perturbation of heme biosynthesis. The provisional, study-specific developmental reference doses derived from fetal or placental endpoints were comparable to or lower than those based on maternal hepatomegaly, suggesting greater developmental sensitivity. These findings reveal structure-dependent fetal liver accumulation and support incorporating fetal-specific endpoints into PFAS risk assessment.

articles.title: Genetic Background and Metabolic Influence on Long-Term Lithium Bioaccumulation in Mytilus Mussels and Their Hybrids
articles.abstract: Abstract Marine mussels are widely used as sentinel organisms in coastal biomonitoring, yet the biological mechanisms controlling the bioaccumulation of emerging metals remain poorly constrained. Climate change and anthropogenic disturbances are reshaping species distributions and contact zones, promoting mussel hybridization that may alter physiological traits and contaminant-handling capacities. Lithium (Li) remains largely overlooked despite its potential toxicity and rapidly increasing global demand. Here, we investigate the influence of critical factors on Li bioaccumulation by mussels combining genetic background and isotopic approaches. Progenies of two Mytilus species and their hybrids were transplanted to the same Atlantic coastal site for 12 months. Over this in situ exposure period, Li concentrations show comparable temporal trends across all progeny groups, with an initial uptake-dominated phase followed by biodilution. Lithium isotope ratios (δ7Li) display a coherent temporal trend across all groups (decrease at early exposure, increase during later growth), and the magnitude of the shift differs slightly among genetic backgrounds. Across samples, δ7Li is coupled to growth-related metrics (dry weight) and inversely related to Li concentrations, indicating a metabolic control on Li isotope compositions of these organisms. Li concentrations are also positively correlated with lithogenic-associated elements (e.g., aluminum), consistent with the influence of particle associated Li. A simplified biodynamic modeling including Li isotopes data further indicates a more efficient Li depuration after 5 months, combined with a relatively stronger contribution from dissolved Li. Overall, growth-related factors emerged as the primary biological drivers of Li concentration and isotope variability, with the relative contributions of dissolved and particulate exposure pathways varying in association with physiological growth. Hybridization may modulate Li bioaccumulation and δ7Li values, but its influence appears secondary and does not compromise the use of Mytilus mussels as bioindicators in established frameworks such as “Mussel Watch”.

articles.title:
Embedding Environmental
Science and Technology into
Sustainability

Divalent Cations
and Chlorine Synergistically Reshape
T6SS-Mediated Microbial Competition in Water Distribution System Biofilms
articles.abstract: Abstract Microbial interactions shape the community structure and function in drinking water distribution system (DWDS) biofilms, yet how the dynamic competition is regulated in biofilms remains poorly understood. Here, we show that divalent cations (Ca2+, Mg2+) and chlorine in drinking water synergistically activate the type VI secretion system (T6SS) in opportunistic pathogens within biofilms. Field-collected biofilms serve as ecological hotspots that selectively enrich specific T6SS-harboring pathogens. Using simulated pipe systems and mutant validation, we further establish that divalent cations and chlorine enhance c-di-GMP signaling to promote T6SS-mediated colonization. This activation stimulates EPS production, whose polysaccharides mitigate T6SS attack, dampening the competitive advantage during mid-stage maturation but allowing gradual resurgence over extended succession. This divalent cation-chlorine-driven interplay shapes ecological succession, selectively retaining T6SS-proficient cells and establishing a “biofilm reservoir effect.” Under chlorine decay, T6SS-active pathogens can be released into bulk water, elevating exposure risks. Conversely, reducing divalent cations via nanofiltration suppresses T6SS across multiple pathogens, limiting reservoir accumulation and release. Our findings identify divalent cation availability as a key environmental signal associated with T6SS-mediated competition, linking water chemistry to pathogen persistence. This work suggests integrating membrane-based divalent cation removal with chlorine management as a chemistry-based strategy to mitigate microbial risks, advancing an integrated water quality paradigm for drinking water safety.

articles.title:
Discovery of Emerging
Aromatic Compounds with High
Potential Risk from Coal-Fired Power Plants
articles.abstract: Abstract Coal combustion releases aromatic compound (AC) mixtures far more complex than the 16 EPA-priority polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). Here, a high-resolution in-house database targeting 104 aromatic compounds prioritized by structural carcinogenicity alerts and structural analogy was developed to complement NIST library matching for screening fly ash, slag, and soil from five coal-fired power plants (CFPPs). This dual-database strategy increased the identification rate by 9.2% and captured 29 compounds previously unreported in the analyzed CFPP-related matrices. A total of 393 ACs spanning 24 structural classes were annotated. Cross-matrix profiling revealed distinct chemical shifts, from primary 1-ring products in slag to secondary chlorinated species in fly ash and ultimately to persistent high-molecular-weight PAHs in soils, suggesting that the observed AC patterns were associated with differences in unit efficiency, end-of-pipe control, and operational history across the five CFPPs. Incremental lifetime cancer risk assessment demonstrated that emerging PAHs contributed 60% of the total carcinogenic risk in fly ash despite comprising only ∼2% of total AC concentrations, with 4-ring compounds identified as the predominant risk drivers. Sensitivity analysis confirmed that assessments restricted to literature-derived toxic equivalency factors underestimate the full carcinogenic potential. These findings reveal a critical yet underrecognized toxic fraction in CFPP fly ash, underscoring the need for risk-oriented management strategies that explicitly incorporate emerging PAHs.

articles.title: Metatranscriptomics Reveals Potential Hybrid Electron Routing in Comammox Nitrospira and NO-Supplemented Cooperation in a Partial Nitritation-Anammox Bioreactor under Dynamic Aeration
articles.abstract: Abstract Intermittent aeration drives partial nitritation-anammox (PN-A) systems, yet how microbiomes regulate aerobic and anaerobic respiration during rapid, oxygen-limited redox shifts remains poorly understood. Here, we applied genome-resolved metatranscriptomics to evaluate transcriptional dynamics in a long-term PN-A bioreactor treating low concentrations of ammonium. Under intermittent aeration, active populations did not follow strict metabolic switching, but instead exhibited complementary regulation by coordinately transcribing aerobic and anaerobic respiratory pathways. Notably, comammox Nitrospira exhibited a severe transcriptional bottleneck, with terminal oxidase expression 2–3 orders of magnitude lower than that of amo and nirK. Gene coexpression and pathway mapping support a novel hybrid electron transport chain where electrons from ammonia oxidation are directly routed to nirK. This alternative electron-transfer route functionally couples energy dissipation with obligatory nitrite detoxification. Concurrently, a severe transcriptional deficit of nirS relative to hdh in anammox Ca. Kuenenia indicates a partial bypass of intracellular nitrite reduction. Collectively, these patterns support a novel nitric oxide-supplemented cooperation: anammox bacteria scavenge extracellular nitric oxide generated by comammox Nitrospira, conserving their own electrons while acting as a vital sink to relieve comammox nitric oxide toxicity. These findings provide a mechanistic blueprint for optimizing advanced PN-A microbiomes through engineered aeration control.

articles.title:
Can the Spatial
Planning of Livestock Production Tackle
Future Nitrogen Pollution in China?
articles.abstract: Abstract Nitrogen (N) pollution from livestock production significantly threatens China’s air and water quality, necessitating innovative solutions to balance food security and environmental sustainability. Studies have mostly overlooked the spatial heterogeneity of N-related environmental impacts and the trade-offs between reducing ammonia (NH3) emissions and N concentrations in water. This study develops a spatially explicit multiscale model system encompassing 13,000 polygons across China to assess soil N balance, NH3 emission intensity, and N concentrations in surface water, aiming to explore integrated spatial-planning (SP) strategies that maximize synergy and minimize trade-offs. Our findings reveal that single-purpose SP scenarios (e.g., reducing NH3 emissions or instream N concentrations) can effectively address one N-related issue but produce substantial trade-offs, leaving >50% of China’s population exposed to at least another N-related problem. However, an integrated SP approach could reduce harmful N exposures for 90% of China’s population while ensuring food security. This approach involves reallocating 14% of livestock production, reducing livestock numbers by one-third relative to the 2050 baseline, and implementing advanced technologies to mitigate N pollution hotspots. Thus, our findings emphasize the importance of spatially explicit N boundaries and multicriteria planning to tackle N pollution in air and water simultaneously, supporting cross-media N management policy-making and region-specific strategies.

articles.title:
Correction to “Application
of the Biological
Toxicity Effect Ratio (BER) Method for Advancing Water Quality Criteria
Derivation”

Cross-Level
Responses of Freshwater Zooplankton to
Micro/Nanoplastics: A Meta-Analysis Integrating Individual- to Community-Level
Evidence
articles.abstract: Abstract Despite the known threats of micro/nanoplastics (MNPs) to freshwater ecosystems, their risks to zooplankton remain poorly resolved because existing evidence is fragmented across biological levels. Consequently, associations between lower-level responses and population- and community-level outcomes remain unclear. Here, we synthesized 3042 research cases from controlled experiments worldwide covering 12 response categories. We found significant overall negative effects of MNPs in systems without predators, with predators, and with predator-conditioned medium. Although molecular-level evidence remains limited, a consistent hierarchical response pattern emerged under predator-absent conditions. We therefore propose a conceptual hierarchical effect pathway (HEP) framework integrating effect sizes and cross-level associations. Within this framework, MNPs exposure was associated with increased ingestion of MNPs, physiological damage, feeding impairment, and reduced activity and defense. These responses formed an upstream tier associated with life-history impairments, including impaired growth and development, reduced reproductive capacity, and reduced survival, although these associations do not establish temporal ordering or causation. Under predator-present conditions, negative population- and community-level effects were also observed. Effect magnitudes also varied with MNPs characteristics, exposure duration, and zooplankton group. Together, the HEP framework clarifies cross-level associations and helps identify informative endpoints and incorporate food-web context into risk assessment of MNPs.

articles.title:
Wastewater
Treatment Plants as Anchor Infrastructure
for Geothermal Energy in Cold Regions
articles.abstract: Abstract Thermal constraints in cold regions suppress biological treatment, increase energy demand, and elevate greenhouse gas emissions of existing wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), and remain a major barrier to the deployment of adequate sanitation infrastructure in many cold-region communities. Where geothermal resources exist, low-enthalpy hydrothermal heat is well matched to this energy gap. Yet, WWTPs are underrecognized anchors for broader geothermal deployment, providing a continuous, weather-independent thermal offtake through which subsurface CAPEX can be amortized. We reframe geothermal-WWTP integration as a system-level enabler that benefits both parts. Using three cascaded configurations for a full-scale WWTP, a rapid techno-economic analysis identifies three trends: energy and carbon savings/revenues alone are insufficient under realistic policy stacks, whereas crediting the upgrade-deferral value of geothermally enhanced treatment makes the project economically favorable across most policy scenarios. Globally, this triple intersection encompasses ∼11,600 catalogued WWTPs serving ∼280 million people, with a further estimate of ∼48 million people in the same regions beyond current service radii. The opportunity is greatest in cold, remote, and underserved communities, where local geothermal resources, treatment intensification, and community-scale demand together carry a case that no single driver could sustain alone.

articles.title:
Pollutant Release
and Transfer Registers (PRTRs) as
a Cornerstone of Global Chemicals Management: Current Gaps and Future
Directions
articles.abstract: Abstract Pollutant Release and Transfer Register (PRTR) systems in different countries are key tools for global chemicals management and an important data source for measuring progress toward achieving Sustainable Development Goal 12 of sustainable consumption and production patterns. However, current implementations face several structural and functional limitations that hinder the broad applicability of the PRTR reporting data. These limitations can be categorized into two main aspects: within-system issues and between-system inconsistencies. Within systems, data gaps can result from limited monitoring of nonpoint sources, incomplete reporting, exemptions due to thresholds and confidentiality agreements, and other similar factors, while data inaccuracies can be caused by estimation errors, duplicated counts, and other related issues. Between systems, differences in chemical lists, threshold settings, emission source types, reporting methods, and other discrepancies can hinder data comparability and integration, limiting the effectiveness of global chemicals management. Addressing these issues, through unified pollutant lists, harmonized reporting methodologies, expanded source coverage, and improved data verification, can significantly strengthen the utility of PRTR systems, advancing an integrated and evidence-based global sound management of chemicals.

articles.title:
Direct Upcycling
of Rare Earth Hyperaccumulator Biomass
into Luminescent CaS:Ce Phosphors
articles.abstract: Abstract Rare earth elements (REEs) are essential to high-tech industries and sustainable development, but traditional mining poses significant environmental challenges. Phytomining, which uses hyperaccumulators to recover REEs from soils or low-grade mines, has emerged as a sustainable alternative; however, the high cost and low efficiency of extracting and purifying REEs from harvested biomass remain major barriers to its practical application. Here, we propose a novel in situ doping strategy to directly convert cerium (Ce)-enriched hyperaccumulator biomass into color-tunable CaS:Ce phosphors and value-added syngas, bypassing complex separation of Ca and REEs. The results show that Ce, Ca, and S could be selectively enriched from hyperaccumulator biomass to the resulting char through solvothermal pretreatment with sulfuric acid and ethanol. Subsequent steam gasification of the char produces Ce-doped CaS phosphors with broad, green-yellow emission and high photoluminescence quantum yields of 18.5–37.4%. Our approach reduces energy use by 33.6%, carbon emissions by 22.4%, and costs by \$2.62 kg–1 biomass, outperforming conventional REE recovery in both environmental and economic sustainability. This strategy provides an environmentally sustainable and economically viable route for high-value utilization of REE-rich biomass, addressing a critical bottleneck in phytomining and advancing its development as a green REE recovery technology.
